texts.full_text: double ligation and bipolar uterine artery coagulation in total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) retrospectively. TLH was performed on 72 patients with selective uterine artery double ligation and on another group of 75 patients who received bipolar uterine artery coagulation, between January 2016 to December 2021 at our institution. The primary outcomes assessed were intraoperative blood loss (IBL), hemoglobin concentration postoperatively day one and three after surgery. Secondary outcome included operative time, hospital length of stay, complications rate during the first month following operation as well as recurrence rates in patients with benign uterine conditions within a year. The data was analyzed using SPSS version 22 software (IBM Corp., Armonk NY). Continuous variables were compared between groups by independent sample T-test and categorical values assessed through Chi-square test. A p-value of less than or equal to .05 indicated statistical significance, while the confidence interval for mean difference in continuous variable was calculated at a level 95%. The results showed that there is no significant differences observed among IBL (p=0.084), hemoglobin concentration postoperatively day one and three after surgery between selective uterine artery double ligation group and bipolar uterine artery coagulation groups, while the operative time was significantly longer in patients who received selective uterine artery double ligation (p=0.002). There were no significant differences found regarding hospital length of stay or complications rate during first month after operation between two study groups. However, there is a trend towards lower recurrence rates among women with benign conditions undergoing TLH and receiving bipolar uterine artery coagulation compared to selective ligation (p=0.053). The follow-up period was 12 months postoperatively in all patients included the analysis of this study. In conclusion, both techniques are effective for controlling intraoperative bleeding during total laparoscopic hysterectomy and have similar outcomes regarding blood loss control, hemoglobin concentration
